analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md, lines 1-4) and a new section in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 48-64). No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage logic changed in the supplied evidence. The docs describe a Gated DeltaNet prompt-prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. It is selected only when it reproduces the stock gated_delta_step output bit for bit, verified by a GPU probe on the first window of each dtype and geometry. The docs also say decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than 16 tokens keep the stock kernel. They add an env var, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED, to disable the new kernel or force packed or rows for A/B measurement. Related threat-model areas are TB-007 (inference engine), T-041 (prefix-cache TTFT oracle) and T-027 (output integrity). The claimed bit-exactness means recurrent checkpoint contents and cache identity should not change, so the T-041 SSD cache posture (HMAC names, TTL, AAD) is unaffected. Faster prefill only slightly shifts TTFT timing, with no new channel in kind. The env override resembles other DARKBLOOM_* performance settings. The docs say it is not passed to the LaunchAgent, and the deadline-qualification environment guard rejects unrecognized DARKBLOOM_* settings. I did not see the actual implementation (GatedDelta.swift, GPU probe, env parsing, configuration.md). So whether the bit-exactness claim holds, whether the probe fails closed, and whether the env var is rejected by DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification cannot be verified here. A follow-up should check those against the code PR, not these docs. No security regression is identifiable from these doc changes.
